subject: SOC 2: Secure SDLC procedural evidence & clarifying Qs
messages:
From: Brightline Capital <security@brightlinecap.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 request: SDLC procedural evidence

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SOC 2 scoping we need a concise evidence package demonstrating your secure SDLC controls (code review, CI/CD gating, secrets management, change approvals). Please provide the following items (or point us to a secured share):

- The current SDLC / PR review policy (most recent revision) and a short changelog showing when the policy last changed.
- A stamped snapshot of PR approval activity for the last rolling 90 days for production-affecting repos (we just need the approver IDs, timestamps, and PR numbers).
- CI/CD job logs for a representative signed build and the pipeline gating decision that promoted it to production (include artifact checksum and the build signature).
- Evidence of secrets handling: rotation policy, KMS key usage logs for the last 30 days, and where ephemeral tokens are minted/rotated.
- Change management tickets or canary rollout notes for one recent production rollout.

If you prefer, upload artifacts to the Drive folder we created (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1BrightlineShare) or send a secure transfer link. Also let us know a good time for a 20–30 minute walkthrough next week.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Security Assurance Lead
Brightline Capital
security@brightlinecap.com

--
Request ID: BR-2027-12-SDLCEV

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Brightline Capital <security@brightlinecap.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 request: SDLC procedural evidence

Alex — appreciate the detailed list. We'll assemble a scoped package and upload to a secured Drive folder by EOD tomorrow. Quick notes / plan:

- Attached items (I will upload these as encrypted artifacts): redwood-sdlc-policy-v1.4.pdf (policy + changelog), pr-approval-snapshot-2027Q3.csv (90-day PR approver export), ci-build-signatures-20271201.tar.gz (signed-build example + checksums), kms-rotation-matrix.xlsx (rotation schedule & current key IDs).
- Marissa, can you add the merge-gate approver log and the pipeline gating runbook?
- Lauren, can you pull the change ticket for the November 2027 rollout we referenced in the SOC scoping call and include the canary notes?

We redact commit-level diffs in the initial package but can provide commit hashes and signed attestations where needed. For cryptographic evidence: our build system signs artifacts with a KMS-backed key (key id: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/rlk/cryptoKeys/rlk-prod-sign). We will include the key fingerprint and an export of the signing event.

Proposed slot for walkthrough: Thu, Dec 2 at 10:00 AM PT — works for us if that matches your team.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments (to be uploaded): redwood-sdlc-policy-v1.4.pdf; pr-approval-snapshot-2027Q3.csv; ci-build-signatures-20271201.tar.gz; kms-rotation-matrix.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightline Capital <security@brightlinecap.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 request: SDLC procedural evidence

On Wed, Dec 1, 2027 at 11:02 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Jonas — appreciate the detailed list. We'll assemble a scoped package and upload to a secured Drive folder by EOD tomorrow. Quick notes / plan:

Thanks @Jonas — I've attached two artifacts to the Drive upload: merge-gate-approvers.log (extract of approver IDs + timestamps for the merge gate service for 2027-09 through 2027-11) and pipeline-gating-playbook.md (playbook we use when a failing canary triggers rollback). A few clarifications for the assessor:

- The PR export includes approver email, GitHub username, timestamp, and whether the approver was an automatic bot (policy enforces two human approvers or 1 human + automated QA check for production tags).
- CI build signatures include a signed SHA256 checksum and the signature envelope; the build signing is performed by our internal CI runner which calls CloudKMS to sign the blob. We will include a signed envelope and the KMS transaction id (tx: ktx-20271201-33a).
- For secrets handling, we will include the KMS access audit snippet (redacted to principal IDs) and the rotation matrix. Note: we do not include raw secret values; only key usage and rotation metadata.

Upload plan: I will place everything into the folder Jonas creates and mark files with ONYX-level encryption tags. If the assessor needs raw logs for forensic stamping we can do a secure SFTP transfer under NDA.

Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments uploaded: merge-gate-approvers.log; pipeline-gating-playbook.md

From: Brightline Capital <security@brightlinecap.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, SIG Assessor <sig-assessor@security-assessor.io>
Date: Fri, 3 Dec 2027 15:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 request: SDLC procedural evidence

Jonas / Marissa — received, thanks. We confirmed the Drive folder and downloaded the artifacts you uploaded: redwood-sdlc-policy-v1.4.pdf, pr-approval-snapshot-2027Q3.csv, ci-build-signatures-20271201.tar.gz, kms-rotation-matrix.xlsx, merge-gate-approvers.log, pipeline-gating-playbook.md. A couple quick follow-ups before the walkthrough:

- Can you provide the signing key fingerprint and the exact KMS transaction id that correspond to the signed build in ci-build-signatures-20271201.tar.gz (we saw ktx-20271201-33a referenced in the envelope but need the KMS operation id and timestamp to reconcile audit logs).
- For the PR approver export, please confirm which Git provider account maps to the approver "infra-automation" bot so we can classify automated approvals vs human approvals.
- We may request a short session (15 min) with your CI team during the walkthrough to validate the artifact signing flow.

If you're available Thu, Dec 2 at 10:00 AM PT we can keep that slot; otherwise Fri Dec 3 at 09:00 AM PT also works.

Thanks — looking forward to the walkthrough.

Alex Chen
Security Assurance Lead
Brightline Capital
security@brightlinecap.com
